Employment Background Checks in Texas (2026 Guide): What Employers Can and Cannot See

Applying for a new job can be stressful enough.

Then comes the background check.

Many job applicants wonder:

  • What shows up on a background check?
  • Can an employer see my criminal record?
  • How far back does a background check go?
  • Can a background check prevent me from getting hired?
  • What are my rights if a background check contains mistakes?

The answers depend on several factors, including the type of background check being performed and the position involved.

If you're applying for a job in Texas, understanding how employment background checks work can help you avoid surprises and protect your rights.

What Is an Employment Background Check?

A background check is an investigation conducted by an employer or third-party screening company to verify information about a job applicant.

Background checks may review:

  • Criminal history
  • Employment history
  • Education records
  • Professional licenses
  • Driving records
  • Credit history (in certain situations)
  • Identity verification

Not every employer checks the same information.

The scope often depends on the position being filled.

Why Do Employers Conduct Background Checks?

Employers commonly use background checks to:

  • Verify qualifications
  • Confirm employment history
  • Evaluate potential risks
  • Protect customers and employees
  • Meet industry regulations
  • Reduce hiring liability

Many employers consider background checks a routine part of the hiring process.

Can Employers Run a Background Check Without Permission?

Generally:

👉 No.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), employers typically must:

  • Provide notice
  • Obtain written authorization

before obtaining certain third-party background reports.

Applicants are often asked to sign a disclosure and authorization form during the hiring process.

What Shows Up on a Background Check?

The answer depends on the type of screening performed.

Common information may include:

  • Criminal convictions
  • Pending criminal cases
  • Employment verification
  • Educational verification
  • Professional certifications
  • Driving records
  • Address history

Different employers may request different levels of screening.

Can Employers See Criminal Records?

Often:

👉 Yes.

Criminal background checks are among the most common employment screenings.

Information may include:

  • Felony convictions
  • Misdemeanor convictions
  • Pending criminal charges
  • Incarceration history

However, not every criminal record automatically disqualifies an applicant.

Many employers evaluate:

  • The nature of the offense
  • How long ago it occurred
  • Whether it relates to the position

How Far Back Can a Background Check Go in Texas?

This is one of the most common questions applicants ask.

The answer depends on:

  • The type of information being reported
  • The salary level of the position
  • Federal and state laws
  • The screening company involved

Because the rules can vary, there is no universal number that applies to every background check.

Can Employers Check Employment History?

Yes.

Many employers verify:

  • Previous employers
  • Job titles
  • Dates of employment

Some employers also attempt to verify:

  • Responsibilities
  • Professional qualifications
  • Employment gaps

However, many former employers provide only limited information.

Can Employers Verify Education?

Yes.

Employers frequently confirm:

  • Degrees earned
  • Graduation dates
  • Schools attended
  • Professional certifications

Education verification is especially common in professional and technical positions.

Can Employers Check Credit Reports?

Sometimes.

Certain employers may review credit information when:

  • Financial responsibilities are involved
  • Regulatory requirements apply
  • The position involves access to financial assets

However, employers generally must comply with federal requirements before obtaining consumer credit reports.

What If a Background Check Contains Errors?

Mistakes happen more often than many people realize.

Examples may include:

  • Incorrect criminal records
  • Mixed identities
  • Inaccurate employment history
  • Outdated information

According to the Federal Trade Commission and consumer reporting agencies, errors in background reports remain a recurring concern for job applicants. (FTC, 2025)

What Happens If an Employer Rejects You Because of a Background Check?

Employers that use third-party consumer reports generally must follow certain procedures before taking adverse action.

This often includes:

  • Providing notice
  • Providing a copy of the report
  • Giving the applicant an opportunity to review the information

Applicants may have the opportunity to dispute inaccuracies.

Can Employers See Expunged Records?

In many situations:

👉 Expunged records are not supposed to appear in routine background checks.

However, the specifics depend on:

  • The type of record
  • The nature of the expunction
  • The screening process involved

Can Employers Check Social Media?

Many employers review publicly available online information.

This may include:

  • LinkedIn profiles
  • Public social media accounts
  • Professional websites

However, employers should still comply with applicable employment laws during the hiring process.

Can a Failed Background Check Lead to Discrimination Claims?

Potentially.

Employers generally must avoid applying background check policies in a discriminatory manner.

For example, federal agencies have recognized that certain hiring practices involving criminal records may create legal concerns if they disproportionately affect protected groups and are not job-related.

The facts of each situation matter.

What Rights Do Job Applicants Have?

Applicants may have rights under laws such as:

  • The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)
  • Anti-discrimination laws
  • State privacy laws
  • Consumer reporting laws

These protections may include rights involving:

  • Notice
  • Consent
  • Access to reports
  • Disputes of inaccurate information

Common Mistakes Applicants Make

Assuming Employers Will Not Verify Information

Many employers conduct verification checks.

Failing to Review Their Own Records

Applicants often discover inaccuracies only after a hiring decision has been made.

Ignoring Background Check Notices

Important rights may depend on timely responses.

Assuming Old Issues Automatically Disqualify Them

Many employers consider the full context of an applicant's background.

Common Myths About Background Checks

"Employers Can See Everything."

Not necessarily. Background checks are subject to legal limitations.

"One Mistake on My Record Means I Can't Get Hired."

Many employers evaluate multiple factors rather than focusing on a single issue.

"Employers Do Not Need My Permission."

Generally, employers must obtain authorization before ordering certain third-party reports.

"Background Checks Are Always Accurate."

Errors can and do occur.

Why Background Checks Matter

Background checks can significantly impact employment opportunities.

For employers, they help evaluate candidates.

For applicants, they can affect:

  • Hiring decisions
  • Career opportunities
  • Professional reputation

Understanding your rights can help you respond appropriately if problems arise.

How The Lange Firm Helps Texas Employees

At The Lange Firm, we help Texas employees and applicants evaluate workplace issues involving:

  • Employment disputes
  • Hiring practices
  • Workplace discrimination
  • Retaliation claims
  • Wage and hour disputes
  • Employment law concerns

Because employees deserve fair treatment throughout the hiring process—not just after they are hired.

Frequently Asked Questions About Employment Background Checks

What shows up on an employment background check?

Background checks may include criminal history, employment verification, education verification, professional licenses, and other relevant information.

Can an employer run a background check without my permission?

Generally, employers must obtain authorization before obtaining certain third-party background reports.

Can a background check contain mistakes?

Yes. Background reports may sometimes contain inaccurate or outdated information.

Can employers see expunged records?

In many situations, expunged records should not appear in routine background checks.

What should I do if a background check is wrong?

You may have the right to review the report and dispute inaccurate information, depending on the circumstances.

Conclusion

Employment background checks are a routine part of the hiring process for many Texas employers.

While they can provide valuable information, applicants also have important rights regarding:

  • Notice
  • Consent
  • Accuracy
  • Fair treatment

Understanding how background checks work can help you navigate the hiring process with greater confidence.

Key Takeaways:

  • Employers often use background checks to verify qualifications and evaluate applicants
  • Criminal history, employment history, and education records are commonly reviewed
  • Applicants generally have rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and other laws
  • Background reports can sometimes contain errors that should be addressed promptly
  • Employers should use background check information in a lawful and non-discriminatory manner
